mid_cta: If your sealed Moravian-district home gets stuffy by February, the ERV sizing visit will show exactly how much fresh air you need.
cta_alt: Or call — we answer ventilation questions before scheduling anything.
local_streets: Main Street historic district, South Side row homes, West Broad Street
local_detail_para: The thick-wall Moravian homes along Main Street and the South Side rows were built tight, and modern weatherization makes them tighter still. When PPL bills drop but indoor air turns stale, that is the signal. An ERV pulls in lake-wind fresh air without losing your heat, and the sizing matters because a too-small unit will not keep up when you have a full house in January. We log existing CFM, count occupants, check the combustion-appliance zone, then spec the exchanger that matches your envelope.

mid_cta: If lake-effect snow buries your furnace vent or the power drops during a January blow, we walk through both before the real cold arrives.
cta_alt: Or call with your model number — we will check the age and vent setup.
local_streets: West 8th Street, Glenwood Hills, Millcreek Township
local_detail_para: The lake-effect corridor from Presque Isle inland to Glenwood Hills and Millcreek can bury a side-wall vent in one overnight blow, and furnaces age faster here because of the wind load and humidity cycling. Penelec outages happen, so we check whether your igniter will restart when power returns or if you will need a manual reset in the dark. The vent inspection covers termination height, screen freeze risk, and intake clearance. If the furnace is past fifteen winters and the heat exchanger has rust shadows, we document it so you can plan a replacement before you are pricing it during a cold snap.

cta_alt: Or text us a photo of your electrical panel — we will confirm capacity.
local_streets: Butler Street corridor, South Side Slopes, Troy Hill
local_detail_para: The steep rowhouse blocks in Lawrenceville, South Side Slopes, and Troy Hill were built before forced air, and retrofitting ductwork through those balloon frames is expensive and invasive. A ductless mini-split gives you zone control without tearing into plaster, and the outdoor condenser mounts on the alley side or a rear deck. Columbia Gas serves most of these neighborhoods, but the electric-only setup means no combustion venting to chase through tight joist bays. We check your panel capacity, run the line set through an existing chase or soffit, mount the wall head, then pull a vacuum and charge the refrigerant.

mid_cta: If your brick home still has the original chimney from the railroad era, the pre-winter tune-up includes a flue safety check you will not get from a flat-rate coupon.
cta_alt: Or call — we answer flue and chimney questions honestly.
local_streets: Chestnut Avenue, 17th Street corridor, Juniata neighborhood
local_detail_para: The brick homes along Chestnut Avenue and 17th Street near the old rail yards still carry original chimneys, and many have been relined or connected to newer furnaces without proper draft testing. During the pre-winter tune-up we pull the burner assembly, photograph the heat exchanger with a scope, check the flue draft with a manometer, and verify the fresh-air supply if the basement was sealed up later. Penelec rates are low enough that electric ignition is common now, but the draft safety still matters because a blocked or deteriorated flue will spill combustion gas. We leave a combustion-analysis printout so you have a baseline for next year.

local_detail_para: The rental blocks along College Avenue, Calder Way, and Park Avenue turn over every May and August, and HVAC maintenance falls through when tenants leave filters unchanged for a full school year. We run pre-lease inspections that document filter condition, thermostat operation, condensate-drain flow, and whether the outdoor coil is packed with cottonwood from the spring bloom. UGI serves most of the borough for gas, and West Penn Power covers electric, so we check both fuel sources if you have a split system. The write-up includes photos and a filter-change log template so you can show the next tenant what normal maintenance looks like.

cta_alt: Or call — we walk through zoning options before quoting anything.
local_streets: West High Street, Dickinson College area, South Hanover Street historic district
local_detail_para: The foursquares along West High Street and South Hanover near Dickinson College have tall ceilings and open stairwells, and a single thermostat on the first floor will never satisfy the second-floor bedrooms. Zoning splits the ductwork with motorized dampers and adds a second thermostat upstairs, or in some cases a separate air handler in the attic makes more sense if the trunk line is too small. UGI supplies gas and Met-Ed covers electric for most of the borough. We measure the existing duct sizes, check the blower capacity, then model whether dampers will balance the system or if you need a supplemental unit to avoid starving the first floor when the second floor calls for heat.
